I would keep my land in the usual wheat-maize rotation, because that is the cropping pattern I trust most in Quzhou County. I know the soils, I know the timing, and at my age I would rather run a steady system than chase a risky crop I do not manage as well. I would put the same land into winter wheat and then summer maize, because that fits our climate, uses the season fully, and gives me grain from both parts of the year. I would use improved seed for wheat and hybrid seed for maize, because I want stable emergence, better disease tolerance, and dependable yield. For field management, I would stay practical: base fertilizer in the ground, topdress nitrogen at the key stage, irrigate only when the crop really needs it, spray only as needed to keep rust, aphids, armyworm, and other common problems under control, and avoid excessive inputs that raise cost without giving me much more grain. I would plough before wheat to set up a clean seedbed, and I would use no-tillage for summer maize after wheat harvest so I can sow quickly and save labor and soil moisture.
